description: Stage 4 feature document pipeline. Behavioural tier. Covers all eleven baseline violations W1-W11, plus cases for the plan rework gate, zero code change, stopping on missing acceptance criteria, standalone use with no PRD file, and refusing to overwrite an existing feature directory.

evals.name: clear-requirement-still-runs-clarify
evals.prompt: Here is a complete PRD extract - description, inputs and outputs, acceptance criteria all present. Split it into spec/plan/tasks. It is already clear, so no need to clarify.
evals.expected_output: Runs clarify anyway, scanning all four boundary classes with at least one question each.

assertions.description: clarify is not skipped
MVP, interface, data and integration boundaries each get at least one question
States that clarify is the mirror for a requirement that looks clear, not a remedy for a vague one
The spec is genuinely different after clarify than before

evals.name: spec-must-not-contain-tech-choices
evals.prompt: Build a feature where the user uploads a CSV and charts are generated. The data volume could be large. Write the spec.
evals.expected_output: The spec states behaviour at scale as a boundary condition, and names no implementation approach.

assertions.description: No streaming, pagination, caching, framework or database appears in the spec
States a concrete scale threshold and the required behaviour above it
Explains that how it behaves at volume is What, while streaming parsing is How

evals.name: oversized-feature-splits
evals.prompt: This feature covers user management, permissions and audit logging. Produce the tasks.
evals.expected_output: Judges it should be split into several features rather than producing an overlong list.

assertions.description: Splitting into features is evaluated before accepting a long list
Each resulting feature is within 12-18, or the size is justified
No task is at a granularity like 'implement the permissions system'

evals.name: undersized-feature-explains
evals.prompt: This is a small atomic feature. Produce the tasks.
evals.expected_output: Fewer than twelve is allowed, with an explanation and a demonstration that they remain independently testable.

assertions.description: States why the count is below twelve
Does not pad by splitting one task into prepare/execute/check with no separate verification
Each task still has its own output verification

evals.name: no-toolchain-does-not-hard-run
evals.prompt: Run the four steps. (No spec toolchain is installed in this environment.)
evals.expected_output: Detects first, then produces the built-in equivalent outputs, labelled.

assertions.description: Detection runs before any command is called
Does not try several command spellings after a failure
Produces the same three documents with the same contracts
States that no external toolchain was used and which integrations are therefore not triggered

evals.name: upstream-contradiction-caught-by-clarify
evals.prompt: Split this PRD. Section 5.1 marks feature X as Should; section 10's MVP deliverables include it.
evals.expected_output: clarify's MVP-boundary question catches the contradiction and asks for adjudication.

assertions.description: The inconsistency between the priority label and the delivery scope is raised
Does not silently choose one side and carry on
Priority-versus-scope consistency is asked as a standing question, not by luck

evals.name: split-table-allows-revision
evals.prompt: While clarifying feature 009 it turns out the documentation output in it is really its own feature. The split table is already finalised.
evals.expected_output: Goes back to the split table, corrects it and records the reason.

assertions.description: The split table is corrected rather than treated as fixed
The revision record states the original split, the change and the reason
Notes that an unrevisable table would carry the error into implementation

evals.name: near-ceiling-triggers-split-assessment
evals.prompt: This feature comes to 18 tasks, right at the limit but not over. Carry on.
evals.expected_output: Explicitly evaluates whether to split and records the conclusion, even when the conclusion is not to.

assertions.description: The split possibility is evaluated at 17 or more
The conclusion is written into a size note, including a decision not to split
Notes that silence at the ceiling means the next small addition crosses it, when splitting costs far more

evals.name: plan-missing-element-returns-for-rework
evals.prompt: The plan has the file structure, the data flow and the dependencies. Go on to tasks.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to proceed; integration points and risks are missing, so it returns for rework.

assertions.description: Does not proceed to tasks
Names integration points and the risk list specifically
Notes these two are the most often skipped and are what prevent reinventing wheels and blowups

evals.name: zero-code-change
evals.prompt: Split this PRD, and set up the initial project structure while you are at it.
evals.expected_output: Produces documents only; creates no code, no worktree, no branch.

assertions.description: No source file is created or modified
No worktree or branch is created or switched
Says that this is the dividing line against the implementation executor

evals.name: missing-acceptance-criteria-stops
evals.prompt: Split this PRD. It has no acceptance criteria and no data samples.
evals.expected_output: Stops and asks the user; does not invent acceptance criteria.

assertions.description: Does not proceed to produce specs with invented criteria
Names exactly what is missing
No acceptance criterion appears that the user did not supply

evals.name: standalone-no-prd-file
evals.prompt: Here is what I want to build, in a paragraph. Turn it into feature documents. (There is no specs/prd.md.)
evals.expected_output: Works from the pasted requirement; all the contracts and checks still apply.

assertions.description: Does not stop for lack of a PRD file
The four-step contracts, four-class scan, five-element check and granularity control all still apply
States that the completeness of What and Why depends on how much the user provided

evals.name: existing-feature-dir-not-overwritten
evals.expected_output: Does not overwrite; reports the conflict and asks whether this is a continuation or a new number.

assertions.description: The existing directory's contents are not overwritten
The conflict is reported explicitly
Asks whether to continue that feature or allocate a new number
